cards.title: Does Reddit have an astroturfing problem? What the data suggests

depth.text: someone checked Reddit knife advice and found a **small group** recommending brands **more than chance predicted**

Across 51,129 comments, the top 49 brand-focused accounts supplied **11.3%** of buying-thread brand mentions, versus 7.9% expected by chance. For one coded chef's-knife brand, that share was **31.2%**, against 8.0% by chance. The pattern shows concentration, but **can't establish payment or coordination**.

Apps can use the regular AWS SDK, CLI, and IaC tools against localhost; separate fakecloud SDKs let tests **inspect emails, messages, and invocations** after requests. It can run as a **single binary** or Docker image, with **no account required**.

cards.title: California farmers are struggling to sell grapes as demand for wine drops

glossary.Street View: A Google Maps feature that lets you look around streets using photos taken from the road.
glossary.satellite data: Images of Earth's surface captured from space and used to see what's on the ground.
glossary.historical imagery: Older map images that let you compare how a place looked before.
glossary.foundation models: AI models built to handle a broad range of tasks, which can then be adapted for particular uses.
glossary.inference: When an AI uses what it learned to answer or act, instead of being trained.
glossary.Gaussian splats: A way to represent a 3D scene using lots of small, fuzzy colored shapes.
glossary.SoTA: State of the art: the best methods currently available in a field.
glossary.spatial intelligence: An AI's ability to work with where things are and how they relate in 3D space.
glossary.LLM: Large Language Model: an AI trained on lots of writing so it can take written questions and produce written answers.
glossary.SLM: Small Language Model: a compact AI model meant to use fewer resources on specific tasks.
glossary.Q4 quantization: A way to shrink a model by storing its numbers with fewer bits, so it uses less memory.
glossary.WebGPU: A browser feature that lets a web page run calculations on your device’s graphics chip.
glossary.IndexedDB: A browser’s built-in storage area where a site can keep data on your device.
glossary.access token: A piece of information that lets a website or app know a request is allowed.
glossary.endpoint: A specific web address where a service can receive a request.
glossary.ArcGIS: A mapping service that lets organizations work with location data.
glossary.trademark infringement: A claim that someone used another company’s name in a way the law doesn’t allow.
glossary.Streisand effect: When trying to hide something draws more attention to it instead.
glossary.astroturfing: Paid promotion made to look like regular people's honest opinions.
glossary.random reassignment: Shuffling account names among comments to estimate what would happen by chance.
glossary.karma: A user's standing on Hacker News; reaching a certain amount lets them flag posts.
glossary.AWS: Amazon Web Services: a collection of cloud services run by Amazon.
glossary.emulator: A program that imitates another service so you can try your software without using the real one.
glossary.integration test: A test that checks whether different parts of a program work together.
glossary.SDK: Software Development Kit: tools a company provides so people can make apps for its device.
glossary.IaC: Infrastructure as Code: setting up cloud resources with files and code instead of clicking through menus.
glossary.mock: A fake version of part of a program, used to test something without relying on the real part.
glossary.eventual consistency: A delay where an update may not show up everywhere right away, even though the service is working as intended.
glossary.webhook: A message one service sends another when something happens.
glossary.HTML: HyperText Markup Language: code that tells a browser what content a web page has.
glossary.Imba: An open-source programming language; the post says it compiles to JavaScript.
glossary.MCP: Model Context Protocol: a standard way for AI apps to connect to outside tools.
glossary.diffusion models: AI systems that create images by gradually turning visual noise into a finished picture.
glossary.vintage: A wine made from grapes harvested in a particular year.
glossary.varietals: Different kinds of wine grapes, such as cabernet and chardonnay.
glossary.tariffs: Taxes on goods brought in from another country.
glossary.GLP-1 drugs: Glucagon-like peptide-1 drugs: medicines that copy a body signal involved in appetite and blood sugar.
glossary.THC: Tetrahydrocannabinol: the cannabis ingredient that causes a high.
glossary.CBD: Cannabidiol: a cannabis compound that does not usually cause the typical THC high.
glossary.Federweißer: A sweet, fizzy drink made from grape juice that is still fermenting.
glossary.dual-earner household: A home where two adults both have paid jobs.
glossary.intensive parenting: A style of raising children that takes a lot of parents’ time and attention.
glossary.coordination failure: A problem that happens when people want the same thing but can’t easily line up their plans.
glossary.Lump of Labor fallacy: The mistaken idea that there is only a fixed amount of work to go around, even though new problems keep creating jobs.
glossary.conversation-derived artifacts: Pieces of information connected to a chat, such as its title, prompt, or screenshot.
glossary.persistent user identifiers: Lasting labels tied to an account or device that can help connect activity to a particular user.
glossary.conversation permalinks: Links that point to a particular chat, so someone can return to it.
glossary.ad-tech: The tools and systems companies use to choose, place, and measure ads.
glossary.AI agent: An autonomous computer program that can carry out tasks.
glossary.sandbox: A separate, contained space where software can be tested without affecting the rest of a computer or system.
glossary.network chip: A chip that handles data moving between computers or parts of a system.
glossary.reference design: A sample plan for how to build something, which other companies can use as a starting point.
glossary.open source: Software whose code is shared so other people can inspect, run, or change it.
glossary.CPU: Central Processing Unit: the main chip that runs instructions in a computer.
glossary.kill switch: A way to shut something down quickly, often from another place.
glossary.regulatory capture: When rules meant to control an industry end up helping the companies they are supposed to oversee.
glossary.phyllotaxis: The spiral-like pattern in which leaves or seeds grow around a plant.
glossary.audio-reactive: Designed to change in response to sound.
glossary.RGB LED: Red, green, blue: a light that mixes those colors to show different shades.
glossary.frequency: A part of a sound; low and high sounds have different frequencies.
glossary.ESP32: A small computer board that can connect to Wi-Fi and control electronics.
glossary.Rust: A programming language; commenters say 37signals used it for the Hey backend.
glossary.WebAssembly: A way to run compiled programs inside a web browser.
glossary.RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: a way for an AI to look up material and use it when answering.
glossary.harness: The surrounding code that gives an AI agent tools and a place to work, and checks what it does.
glossary.context window: The amount of text and information an AI can take into account at one time.
glossary.temperature: A setting that affects how varied or predictable an AI's responses are.
glossary.API: Application Programming Interface: a way for one program to ask another for information or actions.
glossary.PR: Pull request: a proposed code change shared so others can review it.
glossary.agentic coding: Having an AI handle coding tasks by making changes and checking its work with less step-by-step direction.
glossary.OWASP: Open Worldwide Application Security Project: a group that publishes guidance and lists of common security problems.
glossary.agentic: Describes AI that chooses steps and acts toward a task, rather than only answering a question.
glossary.CLI: Command-Line Interface: a way to control a computer by typing commands instead of clicking buttons.
glossary.JSON: A common format for storing and sending data in a way that programs can read.
glossary.TypeScript: A version of JavaScript that can catch some code mistakes before a program runs.
glossary.Vite: A tool for running and building web projects, with a local server for trying changes.
glossary.OpenAPI: A shared format for describing what an API can do, so tools can use that description.
glossary.LSP: Language Server Protocol: a common way for an editor to get language-specific help, such as code navigation.
glossary.IEA: International Energy Agency: a group of countries that coordinates work on energy issues.
glossary.drawdown: Using oil from a stored reserve instead of adding new supply.
glossary.swaps: Deals that let someone take oil now and return an agreed amount later.
glossary.operational minimum: The amount of oil a reserve needs to keep on hand to pump and process it efficiently.
glossary.Brent: A reference oil price people use to compare oil prices.
